ing: plus extra for dusting and thickening
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour with [[1 tsp]] salt. Rub in the cold butter until crumbly, then stir in the cold water to make a dough. Wrap and chill for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] flour, then the stock, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, remaining salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the gravy is very thick. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll out the chilled dough and cut six 5-inch circles to line a muffin tin or pie tins. Press them in.
Fill each base with the cooled meat. Cut six lids from the puff pastry, brush the rims with egg, and press on.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and cut a small steam slit in each.
Bake for 30 minutes until deep golden. Cool 10 minutes, then eat with extra tomato sauce.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the pork, onion, breadcrumbs, one egg, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl until just combined.
Lay the puff pastry sheets on a floured counter. Cut each in half lengthwise to make 4 long strips.
Shape the pork mixture into 4 long logs and place one along the center of each strip.
Brush one long edge of the pastry with beaten egg, fold the pastry over the filling, and press to seal. Crimp with a fork.
Cut each roll into 4 pieces and set them seam side down on the baking sheet.
Brush the tops with the remaining beaten egg and cut two small slashes in each.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and golden. The pork must reach 160°F (71°C) inside. Cool for 5 minutes.

ing: from large eggs, at room temperature
st: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Trace a 9-inch circle on parchment, flip it over, and place on a baking sheet.
Beat the egg whites in a very clean bowl on medium speed until soft peaks form.
With the mixer running, add the sugar one spoonful at a time. Beat for 8 to 10 minutes until the meringue is stiff and glossy and no sugar grains remain when rubbed between your fingers.
Sift the cornstarch over the meringue and add the vinegar and vanilla. Fold gently.
Mound the meringue inside the circle, smoothing the sides and making a shallow dip in the top.
Put it in the oven and lower the heat to 250°F (120°C). Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until crisp and pale.
Turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside with the door closed for [[1 hour]]. Small cracks are normal.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Just before serving, pile it into the dip and top with the strawberries and kiwi.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and line a 9 by 13 inch pan with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat the softened butter and sugar for 4 minutes until fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the milk, and mix until just smooth.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely in the pan, then chill for [[1 hour]] so it is easy to cut.
Cut the cake into 16 squares.
Sift the powdered sugar and cocoa into a bowl. Stir in the melted butter and hot water until the icing is smooth and runny.
Using two forks, dip each square into the icing to coat all sides, let the extra drip off, then roll it in the coconut.
Set them on a rack to dry for [[30 minutes]] before serving.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small pot over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Stir the baking soda into the boiling water, then pour it into the melted butter. It will foam up.
Pour the butter mixture into the dry ingredients and mix well.
Roll level tablespoonfuls of dough into balls and place them 2 inches apart on the sheets. Flatten them slightly.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden. For chewier biscuits take them out earlier.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move to a rack. They crisp up as they cool.
Toast the bread slices in a toaster until golden.
Spread the butter on the toast while it is hot, right to the edges, so it melts in.
Scrape the Vegemite on very thinly. It is very salty and strong, so a little goes a long way.
If you like, lay the cheese slice over one piece and press on the other piece.
Cut into strips or triangles and eat right away.

ing: or all-purpose flour with 4.5 tsp baking powder
st: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Dust a baking sheet or cast-iron pan with flour.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Make a well in the middle and pour in the milk and water. Mix with a butter knife until the dough just comes together.
Knead on a floured counter for only 1 minute. Overworking makes it tough.
Shape into a round loaf about 2 inches tall and place on the baking sheet.
Cut a cross about 1/2 inch deep in the top and brush with a little milk.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool for 10 minutes and serve warm with butter and golden syrup or jam.

ing: about 1.5 lb, split into 4 thin cutlets
st: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally, then pound the cutlets to 1/2 inch thick.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in the flour, dip in the egg, and press into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets 3 minutes per side until golden. They do not need to be cooked through yet.
Place the cutlets on a baking sheet. Top each with a slice of ham, then a few spoonfuls of tomato sauce.
Cover with the shredded mozzarella.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the cheese bubbles and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Serve hot with fries and a green salad.
Let the butter sit out until very soft so it spreads without tearing the bread.
Lay the bread slices out on a board.
Spread butter right to the edges of each slice. Edge-to-edge butter is what makes the sprinkles stick.
Pour the sprinkles onto a plate in a flat layer.
Press each buttered slice face down into the sprinkles and shake off the extra.
Cut each slice into 4 triangles, or 2 triangles for a classic look, and serve.

ing: 6 oz each, skin on, or sea bass
st: Take the fish out of the fridge for 10 minutes. Pat the fillets very dry, especially the skin.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Place the fillets skin side down and press gently for 10 seconds so they stay flat. Cook 4 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Flip the fish. Add the butter and garlic to the pan.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes more, spooning the garlic butter over the fish, until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Squeeze the lemon juice into the pan and swirl.
Serve the fillets with the pan sauce and lemon wedges.

ing: finely sliced, or 0.5 tsp chili flakes
ground; or extra lemon zest with a pinch of dried lemongrass
st: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, mix the olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, chili, lemon myrtle, and salt.
Add the shrimp and toss until coated. Marinate in the fridge for [[20 minutes]].
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water while the shrimp marinate. Thread 4 or 5 shrimp on each skewer.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and curled with firm flesh.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the top and sprinkle with parsley. Serve hot.

ing: a double shot, from the coffee beans
st: Grind [[18 g]] of coffee beans fine and pack them into the espresso machine portafilter. Tamp down firmly and level.
Pull a double shot of espresso, about 2 fl oz in 25 to 30 seconds, into a small warmed cup.
Pour the cold milk into a small steaming pitcher, filling it only a third.
Steam the milk with the wand tip just below the surface for 3 to 4 seconds to add a little air, then submerge to swirl it. Stop at about 140°F (60°C).
Tap the pitcher on the counter and swirl to make the milk glossy and smooth, like wet paint.
Add sugar to the espresso if you want it, then pour the milk in a steady stream, finishing with a thin layer of microfoam on top.
